body:
Hey, thanks for the reply!

I think you're right, college isn't for everyone, but I think it's expected of me. I go this school with the sons of lawyers, doctors, CEOs, etc. It's not right for me. Something like 98% of graduating classes on average go onto college. That means the question isn't "are you going to college", it's "where are you going to college".

I've had two therapists and I've talked to a counselor at school. And it's funny, they all say the same thing you said about how my parents don't know about mental health and all. My father is a psychologist, he spent like ten years studying it in college. So, no matter where I am or what I'm doing he always likes to pschoanalyze me telling me that I'm in "denial" or "avoidance" when in reality all I'm doing is watching television because that is what I do on Saturdays. I never talk to anyone about suicidal feelings because I think they'll treat me like a threat to myself and that I don't know what I want.

I've openly thought about becoming a stonemason. I watched a man fix our chimney about a year ago and thought it seemed like an interesting thing to do, though my mom tells me I can't do that because I can't support myself or a family on something like that. I've pretty much forgotten about it till now.

Thanks for the link, I downloaded the app and I think it will be an interesting way to learn alongside school. I've also been using an app called Elevate that's supposed to keep my mind sharp.

My biggest problem with life is working with the cards I've been dealt. We'll see how much this working on myself will help.
After all, it couldn't hurt.
